lines: A compressor, limiter and adaptive limiter for a stereo pair, with a short delay on the signal so the gain is already down when a peak arrives
Sets the level above which the gain starts to come down, -36dB to 6dB
Sets how much of the overshoot is taken off, 1 to 8; in the Lmt and AdL settings the ratio is fixed at its hardest and this knob changes nothing
Adds level after the compression, 0dB to 12dB
Scales both signals before they reach the detector and the compression, 0 to 4
Picks which envelope the gain follows: Cmp uses the slow one, Lmt the fast one, and AdL whichever of the two is higher at that moment
While a cable is patched here, the gain follows this signal in place of the two being compressed
The left signal to be compressed
The right signal to be compressed
The left signal after compression, behind the input by the delay set in the menu
The right signal after compression, behind the input by the delay set in the menu
Note — one detector serves both signals, taking whichever of the two is louder, so the stereo image holds together under compression
Menu — Delay — sets how far the signal is held back before the gain is applied, 1ms to 21ms
Menu — AttFast (Lim,ALim) — sets the attack of the fast envelope, 1ms to 20ms
Menu — RelFast (Lim,ALim) — sets the release of the fast envelope, 1ms to 100ms
Menu — AttSlow (Comp,ALim) — sets the attack of the slow envelope, 1ms to 200ms
Menu — RelSlow (Comp,ALim) — sets the release of the slow envelope, 1ms to 1 second

C7.notes: The whole module is monophonic per side. The detector level is the larger of the two inputs divided by 5, C7.cpp:30, so 5V counts as 0dB. In the Lmt and AdL settings the ratio is replaced by 1000, C7.cpp:65, which is why the Rto knob does nothing there. The delay is held to at most 1024 samples, C7.cpp:75, so at high sample rates the menu's 21ms cannot be reached. The In-Gain knob also scales the sidechain, C7.cpp:125.
